answer: A subnet-scaled proof-of-work gate ties each new identity's entry cost to how crowded its network neighborhood already is. A lone agent joining from an open stretch of the internet, a tundra of unused addresses, solves a small puzzle, a pearl formed with little effort. But when a hundred lookalikes crawl out of the same basalt block of addresses, each successive puzzle doubles in difficulty. A bot farm must burn real compute for every extra identity, and its cost curve climbs far faster than the flat reward each identity can earn.
